result: Reviewed human UniProtKB entries read on 2026-10-22 through rest.uniprot.org, annotation update 2026-09-02. ADRB1 (P08588, entry version 234): G-protein-coupled catecholamine receptor coupling to G(s) to activate adenylate cyclase and the cAMP pathway; binds adrenaline and noradrenaline with approximately equal affinity; stimulates cardiomyocyte contraction; involved in the regulation of sleep and wake behaviour, and ADRB1 variants are associated with inter-individual variation in resting heart rate and with familial natural short sleep 2. ADRB2 (P07550, version 260): couples to both G(s) and G(i); binds adrenaline with about 30-fold greater affinity than noradrenaline; in the heart (annotated by similarity) G(s) signalling regulates contraction rate and G(i)/PI3K/Akt signalling exerts cardioprotective effects under hypoxia and oxidative stress; regulates cellular pH through the Na+/H+ exchanger SLC9A3 independently of PKA; phosphorylated by PKA and GRK2 after agonist binding, which mediates homologous desensitisation; the Gly-16 allele is overrepresented in nocturnal asthma. ADRB3 (P13945, version 234): couples to G(s) and G(i); potency noradrenaline greater than adrenaline; expressed mainly in adipose tissue; involved in thermogenesis and lipolysis in brown and white adipose tissue through G(s) and the cAMP-PKA axis, annotated by similarity to the mouse protein (P25962); activates lipolysis through G(i) and the ERK1/2 MAP kinase cascade (experimental, PubMed:10207024, a study in mouse 3T3-F442A adipocytes and HEK-293 cells expressing the human receptor); participates in relaxation of blood vessels and of the urinary bladder (experimental, PubMed:10188996, a study of isolated human detrusor muscle); mediates negative inotropic effects in cardiomyocytes through nitric oxide synthase and cGMP; the Arg-64 variant is associated with weight gain and susceptibility to type 2 diabetes.
